conviction_note: Q3 was guided as a no-land-sale quarter, so the reported number should land roughly where it was guided. The print turns on whether the ~$100M 2026 consolidated net income guide survives. That guide needs about $75M or more of net income in Q4, from ~28.5 Great Park acres plus ~20 Valencia acres all closing in Q4. Every large builder that reported after FPH's July call described weaker demand (Lennar cut its delivery target, KB said conditions weakened since June, Toll called demand challenging). That leans slightly negative (p_up 45), but it is a proxy and management already hedged 'subject to market conditions'. The stock sits 7% off its 52-week low with little short interest, so the lean is small. abs_move 5.5 is the 5.0% median reaction lifted slightly for the guidance risk. The findings sum (-1.1) is about twice the scaled number (-0.55). That is because the guidance proxy carries its full size as a finding, while p_up only leans five points off 50.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS -$0.04 on revenue of $8.61M, from a single source: MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/five-point-nysefph-shares-gap-up-after-strong-earnings-2026-07-24/. The same $8.61M also appears as the Q1 and Q2 estimate, so it is probably a stale placeholder. Earnings Whispers shows no estimate (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/FPH). The real bar is the company guide: about $100M of 2026 consolidated net income, H1 at $25.0M, remaining land sales expected in Q4 (Q2 8-K ex-99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001574197/000157419726000025/ex-991xfphx63026x8k.htm). The EPS/revenue bar is not sourced to two agreeing estimates, so every finding is capped small. The +30% print_vs_bar is against the $8.61M revenue placeholder: recurring management fees plus Hearthstone fees ran about $15M in Q2 before land-sale reversals, so a Q3 with no land sales should still clear $8.61M. It says nothing about the line the stock trades on.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1% of float and days to cover about 2.7 (Equibles, data as of 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/FPH). Days to cover ranged roughly 1.5-3.9 over 2025-26. The short is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism against a negative. No usable option chain: ATM legs are not two-sided, total open interest 27, skew null. The market makes no directional statement here. Tape: -3.28% over 20 days, -27.5% from the 52-week high and +7.4% above the 52-week low. Today the stock is +6.3% intraday ($4.30 to ~$4.57) with ITB +4.7% the same day (Yahoo chart), so the move into the print looks sector-wide, not company-specific.

findings.finding: The company itself guided Q3 2026 as a quarter with no land sales. The Q2 release and call said remaining 2026 land sales 'will occur during the fourth quarter', and Q1 (also no land sales) was a ~$5.0M consolidated loss. So Q3 should print a small loss against Q3 2025, which carried $257.7M of Great Park residential land sales. The YoY headline will look much worse, but it sits inside what the company told the market to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, also a guided no-land-sale quarter with a small loss: +0.99%. Q3 2025, with the $257.7M land sale: -1.03%. The reported quarter has not been what moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The company said it out loud, and consensus (-$0.04, single source) already expects a loss. If it were unpriced, the stock would have sold off after the July call, but it gapped up +4.4% that day. The only unpriced piece is headline/algorithmic optics on the YoY comparison against the Q3 2025 land sale (https://www.ocbj.com/oc-homepage/fivepoint-pushes-on-with-irvine-land-sales/, 2025-11-10).
findings.independence: Q1 2026 loss implied by the same 8-K (H1 $25.0M minus Q2 $29.9M). The Q4 2025 call said earnings would be weighted to H2 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/five-point-q4-earnings-call-033855684.html, 2026-01-29). Both are company documents, so this is not independent of the company.

findings.finding: The $100M FY2026 consolidated net income guide needs about $75M+ of net income in Q4 after H1 at $25.0M and a likely Q3 loss. All of it rests on ~28.5 Great Park acres across five builder programs still 'in due diligence and contracts' plus the ~20 Valencia acres planned for 2026 (no 2026 Valencia land sale has been announced). Every large builder that reported after FPH's July 23 call described weaker demand: Lennar Q3 orders -9% with its FY delivery target cut to 80-81k (2026-09-16), KB Home orders -12% with conditions 'weakening since June' (2026-09-22), Toll calling demand 'challenging' (2026-08-18). That raises the risk on tonight's call of a Q4 slip into 2027 or a cut to the $100M guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moves this name. Q4 2025, when the first $100M 2026 guide (about 45% below 2025's $183.5M) was given: -5.01%. Q2 2026, guide held plus a $159.3M land sale: +4.39%. Q2 2025: -14.93%. Q1 2025: +41.63%. On the Q2 call management promised more detail on builder land deals at this Q3 call, so tonight is where the Q4 pipeline gets disclosed.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -27.5% from its high and 7% above its 52-week low, and management already hedged 'subject to market conditions'. If the market fully expected a cut, the stock would trade well below its pre-guide level with no bid into the print. Instead it is +6% today with the builders. No sell-side preview with a revised FY number could be found, and the only consensus is a stale placeholder, so nobody has visibly marked the guide down.
findings.independence: These are proxies, not FPH's own numbers: Lennar 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920760/000162828026062287/ex991-2026831x8kq3.htm), KB Home 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000795266/000079526626000068/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm), Toll Q3 (https://finviz.com/news/383466/toll-brothers-reports-fy-2026-third-quarter-results). The counterweights are recorded here and reflected in the size: Toll's Pacific segment was the only one flat-to-up (+0.7%) and Toll said luxury buyers held up, which is the Irvine price point. FPH also said it would adjust deal structures rather than cut land value. Last year's Q3 release disclosed 113 homesites closed after quarter end (OCBJ, 2025-11-10), so an October closing could also be announced tonight and push the other way.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-25 FPH extended its Development Management Agreement with the Great Park Venture (Heritage Fields El Toro) from 2026-12-31 to 2028-12-31. The base fee stays at $13.5M/yr plus 9% incentive compensation on Venture distributions, with an incentive payment and a 6.75% tail if not extended after 2028. This locks in the main recurring fee stream for two more years.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print reaction on the DMA. The 8-K went out 2026-09-30, and the stock drifted from $4.72 (9/29) to $4.68 (9/30) to $4.58 (10/1), so the filing itself was not bought.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public in an 8-K, but no wire story carried it and the tape ignored it. If it were priced, the stock would have firmed on 9/30, but it fell. The call may frame it as part of the 2027-28 fee outlook. It is small because ~$13.5M/yr was already the run-rate, and the extension may defer an incentive payment the old end-2026 termination could have triggered.
findings.independence: None. This is a single document.

findings.finding: FPH bought back 623,432 Class A shares for $3.1M in Q2 2026 and management called the shares attractive. At about $4.57 the equity is worth roughly $680M against $348M of cash and $566M of liquidity (net debt to capitalization 4.2%), so a larger buyback or authorization update on the call is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 print, where the buyback was first quantified, reacted +4.39%, but it also carried a land sale and the guide was held, so the buyback cannot be isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is small ($3.1M a quarter against a ~$680M market cap), and management said it is balancing buybacks against Hearthstone growth, so nobody expects an acceleration. A larger number would be news. There is no document saying one is coming, so the size is small.
findings.independence: The call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15278768186156032) has Tobler saying the shares look attractive but that buybacks are balanced against Hearthstone. That is the same company source and it cuts both ways.

findings.finding: FPH is +6.3% intraday on 2026-10-22 ($4.30 to ~$4.57, 5-day +6.7%) going into tonight's print, alongside ITB +4.7% the same day. Entry at today's close therefore starts after a sector rally has already lifted the stock, which leaves less room for a guide that is merely held.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history on run-ins. Q3 2025 printed a $257.7M land sale and still fell 1.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is not mispricing. It is a sector move that the stock's own print has not yet tested. If the rally were company-specific there would be FPH news, and none was found. A rates-driven builder rally is also mildly supportive for Q4 land demand, which offsets part of this, so it is sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: Entrada South and Valencia Commerce Center entitlement sales are not expected to start until early 2028. Candlestick grading was due to start in Q3 2026, with large campus users being courted. These are long-dated value drivers and nothing about them closes inside the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or option anchor to agree or disagree with. The slight negative lean on guidance cuts against today's +6% sector-driven run-in and against a stock already 7% off its 52-week low, which is why p_up stays at 45 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar has a single, likely stale source; the reported-quarter finding lands inside what the company guided): reported-quarter finding -0.3 -> -0.2
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission from peers' prints that FPH has not confirmed, filed small): guidance finding -1.5 -> -1.2
Rule 7 (looked up short interest before the negatives): about 1% of float, 2.7 days to cover, not crowded, so no further shrink
